entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv6526"/><title type="x-s2">PSALM 89</title> <title type="x-s3"><reference osisRef="Ps.89.1-Ps.89.52">Psa 89:1-52</reference>. Of Ethan--(See on <reference osisRef="Ps.88.1">Psa 88:1</reference>, title). This Psalm was composed during some season of great national distress, perhaps Absalom's rebellion. It contrasts the promised prosperity and perpetuity of David's throne (with reference to the great promise of <reference osisRef="2Sam.7.12-2Sam.7.17">2Sa 7:12-17</reference>), with a time when God appeared to have forgotten His covenant. The picture thus drawn may typify the promises and the adversities of Christ's kingdom, and the terms of confiding appeal to God provided appropriate prayers for the divine aid and promised blessing.</title> <div sID="gen10000" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv6526"/><hi type="bold">1. mercies--</hi>those promised (<reference osisRef="Isa.55.3">Is 55:3</reference>; <reference osisRef="Acts.13.34">Ac 13:34</reference>), and--<div eID="gen10000" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen10001" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">faithfulness--</hi>that is, in fulfilling them. <div eID="gen10001" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv6530"/><div sID="gen10008" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv6530"/>8-14. To illustrate His power and faithfulness examples are cited from history. His control of the sea (the most mighty and unstable object in nature), and of Egypt (<reference osisRef="Ps.87.4">Psa 87:4</reference>), the first great foe of Israel (subjected to utter helplessness from pride and insolence), are specimens. At the same time, the whole frame of nature founded and sustained by Him, Tabor and Hermon for "east and west," and "north and south," together representing the whole world, declare the same truth as to His attributes. <div eID="gen10008" type="x-p"/>
